text:
Jordan P.: Hey folks, Jordan here starting on Platform today. Stuck on SSO/MFA flows. When I try to register my YubiKey as a passkey in Okta it errors with 'Authenticator already registered' even though I've never enrolled before. Also no 1Password invite yet. Who do I ping?
People Ops: Welcome Jordan! :wave: Tagging IT Support to triage Okta and 1Password. @it-support can you take a look?
IT Support: Hi Jordan, welcome. Can you share whether you're on a company device and which browser? Also paste the exact Okta message if possible.
Jordan P.: Using company MacBook Air (seeded today), macOS 14.0, Safari 16.6. Error dialog copy: "Registration failed: Authenticator already registered for this user". Browser console shows:
```
OktaWebAuthnError: AuthenticatorAlreadyRegisteredError: credential ID conflict
id: err-0x7f2
```
Nina (eng): fwiw, Safari sometimes keeps stale credentials tied to an old test account. If you ever tried a personal Okta dev org it can conflict. Did you previously register a passkey or use a YubiKey on this machine?
Jordan P.: I registered a YubiKey years ago for a personal account, maybe it's interfering. I didn't think it would affect the corporate flow.
Security: That can happen. Credential IDs are scoped to the RP ID (okta domain) but browser stored keys can cause conflicts. @it-support we typically clear existing WebAuthn keys or use a different RP tag.
IT Support: Two options: 1) Temporarily lift device-trust so you can enroll via Okta Verify (mobile) while we clean up WebAuthn, or 2) we can walk you through removing old credentials from Safari and re-register the YubiKey. Which do you prefer?
Jordan P.: I'd like to use the YubiKey for future-proofing. Happy to remove old creds if it's safe.
IT Support: OK. Steps for Safari: Preferences > Privacy & Security > Manage Website Data > search for "okta" and remove related entries, then restart Safari and try again. If that doesn't work we can run `security` commands to list and remove WebAuthn entries. I'll standby.
onboard-bot: Account provisioning update 1 Nov 2026: Okta: invite_sent status=pending, GoogleWorkspace: invite_sent, 1Password: seat_pending
Jordan P.: Did the Manage Website Data clear and reboot. Tried again and now the error is different: "NotAllowedError: The operation is not allowed" when touching my YubiKey.
IT Support: Are you touching the correct key and is it set to CTAP2/2FA mode? Also check System Settings > Security > USB Accessories restrictions (macOS can block).
Jordan P.: USB accessories is allowed. YubiKey firmware is up-to-date. I also tried in Chrome and saw same NotAllowedError. Console:
```
DOMException: NotAllowedError: The user or device refused the request
ctx: navigator.credentials.create -> okta-webauthn
```
Security: Sometimes the YubiKey's resident key policy can block creation if existing resident credentials exist. If you have a personal key with resident credentials that could prevent new RP entries. You can use YubiKey Manager to inspect and remove resident keys. If you prefer, we can issue a temporary Okta Verify fallback while you do that.
Jordan P.: Can we do the fallback for now so I can access Drive and slack? I can try YubiKey Manager later.
People Ops: Absolutely. @it-support please enable temporary device-trust for 8h and send a one-time Okta Verify SMS.
IT Support: Done 1 I added you to temp-device-trust (8h) and resent the Okta verification. Try the SMS code and confirm.
Jordan P.: SMS worked, enrolled Okta Verify, Drive and Slack are accessible. Thanks. What's the plan for 1Password seat?
IT Support: 1Password seat was queued to the wrong alias earlier; I've reassigned it to jordan.p@redwood.com and resent the invite. You should get it shortly.
Jordan P.: Invite arrived and I can sign in. After work I'll run YubiKey Manager and remove old resident keys, then try the YubiKey enroll again.
Nina (eng): Ping me if you want a quick pairing to test repo access and SSH keys. I can add your public key to the temporary dev host.
Jordan P.: Thanks Nina, will do. Big thanks to IT and People Ops for the quick lifts! :tada:
IT Support: Marking this temp-device-trust exception as audited; please file a quick note if you notice anything odd when you remove your resident keys.
Security: Reminder: if you remove resident keys, confirm you still have access to any personal accounts that used that key. We don't want accidental lockouts.
Jordan P.: Will do. All set for now. Appreciate the help!
